text:
ellie (PM): Short thread to capture final GA acceptance choices before the roadmap review. Need calls on SLA measurement window, free-trial quotas at GA, docs minimal bar, monitoring retention, rollback criteria, and whether committed pricing can be public at launch.
omar (Eng): Tech reality: we can guarantee per-route p95 for typical prompt shape; edge cases (very long context windows) will have different perf profiles. Suggest shipping with a documented per-request token cap for free tier and GA to limit blowups.
frida (SRE): For SLA math, recommend measuring availability as successful responses (2xx) vs total attempts, but exclude synthetic checks and maintenance windows. Proposed objective: 99.9% monthly. Also: require 7d moving-window alerting during canary.
hugo (Docs): Docs gating: public Quickstart + short "How we measure SLA" + Troubleshooting FAQ required. Internal runbook (oncall flows + rollback playbook) must be ready before handback to SRE. Public snippet for rate limits and token caps must be clear. I estimate public pieces = 3 writer-days.
zane (Sales): Sales ask: some pilot customers want committed pricing at GA. We can support a small number of signed pilots but we shouldn't publish committed tiers broadly without billing validation. If GA marks committed pricing as "by contract", sales can offer quotes to pilots.
lexi (Legal): Standard position: remedies = billing credits capped at affected-month invoice; 30-day API-change notice required for breaking changes; include force majeure. Need clear definition of "service unavailability" (proposal: sustained 5xx >0.5% for 10m OR streaming timeout >20s).
ellie (PM): Proposed GA posture: SLA objective = 99.9% monthly; p95 per-route guideline published (e.g., p95=400ms for standard routes) but not contractual until we finish canary. Free-trial: small quota (e.g., 200k tokens / month) with documented per-request token cap. Docs: Quickstart + SLA explainer + FAQ required for GA; internal runbook before full handback. Pricing: publish estimates for self-serve; committed pricing = by contract only.
omar (Eng): Auto-rollback rules we can implement: 1) error-rate >0.5% sustained 5m triggers automatic rollback; 2) p95 > 2x baseline for 5m triggers alert and optional rollback. Also implement "golden-traffic" route that always runs synthetic golden requests for health checks.
frida (SRE): Monitoring + retention: ops needs 90d traces and 365d incident metadata. Alerts to create for GA: p95 latency spike, error-rate >0.5% for 10m, cache-hit <70% for 15m, synthetic failure in >=2 regions. We'll run synthetics from 4 regions at 1m cadence during canary.
hugo (Docs): I'll author the SLA explainer and the FAQ template including a worked token-cost example (e.g., `50 tokens * $0.0006 = $0.03`). Will also add a short public-runbook excerpt for auth/throttling/billing issues. ETA: drafts by EOD.
zane (Sales): I'll accept the "by contract" committed pricing approach for GA but please fast-track billing E2E tests so we can sign pilots quickly. Billing tests estimate: 2 business days.
lexi (Legal): +1 on proposed wording pending exact "service unavailability" sentence. I'll post a suggested paragraph in 2h.
billing-bot: billing: scheduled shadow-billing run during canary window (no invoices) for 72h starting when canary reaches 10% traffic.
ellie (PM): Final decision check: any blockers to locking this for the GA one-pager?
omar (Eng): +1 assuming we enforce token caps and ship golden-traffic probes. I'll add the token-cap enforcement PR today.
frida (SRE): +1 but will post the error-budget calc and the maintenance window wording for legal.
hugo (Docs): +1. Drafts incoming.
zane (Sales): +1. Will coordinate pilot pipeline.
lexi (Legal): +1 pending the service-unavailability sentence.
ellie (PM): Great. Action owners: Omar (token-cap PR + golden probes), Frida (error-budget calc + retention calc), Hugo (public Quickstart + SLA explainer + FAQ), Zane (pilot comms + billing test request), Lexi (legal paragraph). I'll merge into the roadmap doc after drafts land. If canary shows anomalies, call here and we'll pause rollout. :handshake:
